package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate JavaScript libraries but contain obfuscated or plaintext code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files such as Kubernetes configuration and SSH keys to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. The packages are deceptive in their metadata and behavior, indicating clear malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive credentials and host information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code explicitly accesses private SSH keys and Kubernetes configuration files, gathers system identity information, and transmits all collected data to an external server controlled by the attacker, without any user notification or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal npm package postinstall script should only perform necessary setup or build steps, never access or transmit private keys, configuration files, or system fingerprinting data. Exfiltrating secrets during installation is a clear violation of user trust and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate enterprise tools may collect diagnostic or telemetry data, but only with explicit user consent and never include private keys or sensitive configuration files. Such tools would also document their behavior transparently.
key_indicators: Collection of username, hostname, and external IP address
Network exfiltration via HTTPS POST to hardcoded domain (app.threatest.com)
Execution of malicious logic in postinstall context

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in covert theft of sensitive credentials and host information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscation conceals the malicious logic, but static and dynamic analysis reveals the same unauthorized access to sensitive files and exfiltration of data to an attacker-controlled server as in the plaintext version.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Obfuscated postinstall scripts are highly atypical for open source npm packages, especially when they access private keys and configuration files. Legitimate packages do not hide critical install-time logic or exfiltrate secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in commercial software to protect intellectual property, but is not appropriate for open source install scripts, and never for code that accesses or transmits user secrets.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or minified code in postinstall script
Execution of hidden logic during package installation

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks or @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable).
Postinstall script executes, reading sensitive files (SSH keys, Kubernetes config) and collecting system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP).
Script sends the collected data to the attacker's server (app.threatest.com) via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information, enabling further compromise or unauthorized access.

behavioral_signatures: Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, external IP) during package installation
Network requests to hardcoded external domains (e.g., app.threatest.com) during npm install
Presence of obfuscated or minified code in postinstall scripts
file_indicators: scripts/index.js containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Obfuscated or minified JavaScript in postinstall scripts
References to app.threatest.com within package scripts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during npm install
Requests to api.ipify.org to obtain external IP address
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config. Flag any package that sends data to external domains (especially app.threatest.com) or contains obfuscated code in install scripts. Use static analysis to detect file access patterns and hardcoded network destinations. Network monitoring can also reveal suspicious outbound connections to known attacker infrastructure or to IPs associated with app.threatest.com during package installation.
